Decoding the PROCTITLE hex: "vim /etc/systemd/system/auditf.service". The log shows the vim editor (running as root via sudo-like elevation from user "john") deleting its swap file ".auditf.service.swp" in /etc/systemd/system/, which is the typical cleanup when a file is edited and closed normally. The file being edited is a systemd unit named "auditf.service", which is notable because it mimics an audit-related service name and systemd unit files in /etc/systemd/system are a common persistence location. However, editing a unit file with vim as root is a routine administrative action, and the deletion of a swap file is an expected side effect of closing vim cleanly. The evidence alone does not show a malicious payload, a service being enabled, or any suspicious network activity.
